{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against 18 playbook rules. The draft is unusually favourable to us: 16 of 18 rules are met, including the critical items (Vendor indemnification at § 20 and IP/Customer Data ownership at § 14), as well as assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), termination for convenience (§ 9.4/§ 29.4), audit (§ 22), governing law and venue (§ 28), renewal and uplift (§ 8), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19) and insurance (§ 18). The Agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation, MFN or minimum-volume obligation on us, and the only MFN in the document (§ 7.6) runs in our favour.

Two deviations require change before signature, and both sit in walk-away territory notwithstanding their nominal severity ratings:

1. **Limitation of liability cap base (§ 21.1).** Structure and carve-outs are fine, but "Fees" is defined at § 1.5/§ 1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form. The cap is therefore an illusory USD 12,000 rather than twelve months' fees, well below our six-month floor.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7).** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, would exceed remaining contract value in roughly seven weeks. This is a payment-delay penalty, not an early-termination fee, so it cannot be brought within the fallback.

We recommend proceeding on the basis of two targeted redlines; the balance of the document needs no comment.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 | Meets preferred position in full; indemnities are Excluded Claims under § 21.3. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 | Customer owns Data and Deliverables; perpetual licence to embedded Vendor Technology (§ 13.2). |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 | Free Customer assignment; § 24.4 bars Vendor repricing/termination on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 | § 12.3 affirmatively confirms no exclusivity; § 12.4 restraint runs against Vendor. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 | Affiliates and contractors covered; revocation limited to uncured material breach (§ 13.3). |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 | No field-of-use or competitive restriction on Customer. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 | § 9.4 plus 30 days' notice (§ 29.4); refund of prepaid Fees, no exit fee. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, Vendor cost, no system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 | New York law, New York County courts; no arbitration provision. |
| Medium | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability** | **Deviation** | **§ 21** | **Cap base narrowed to the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee; below the six-month floor.** |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 | § 7.6 MFN runs in our favour; not redlined. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2 | No minimum quantity; declining further Orders expressly not a breach. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 | No no-hire covenant; § 12.3 preserves our hiring freedom. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 | Six months' assistance at expiring rates; return within 30 days, deletion only after confirmation. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 | Professional-services and 90-day conformity warranties; tiered remedy, non-exclusive. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 | Matches model limits, including USD 5M cyber; term plus one year. |
| Low | **LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 7.7** | **15% of annual Fees per week for a 10-day payment delay; fails preferred and fallback.** |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

Both deviations are characterised in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions to signature:

- **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** Because "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as only the § 1.6 one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, and § 21.1 further narrows it to the first Order Form, recurring subscription and services charges fall outside the cap base. Our position: reset the cap to the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, and broaden the payment-obligations carve-out in § 21.3. Mutuality (§ 21.1), the mutual consequential-damages exclusion (§ 21.2) and the Excluded Claims list (§ 21.3) are acceptable and stay as drafted.
- **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** At fifteen percent of annual Fees per week following a ten-day payment delay, the charge would exceed remaining contract value in roughly seven weeks and is triggered by a minor breach. Our position: no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer; replace with simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts, consistent with the interest reference in § 7.3. Note the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) is unavailable here because this is a payment-delay charge, not a termination fee.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. Issue the two redlines with `[Playbook]` comments: (a) § 21.1 cap reset to the greater of trailing twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with a broadened § 21.3 payment-obligations carve-out; and (b) § 7.7 negated in favour of simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts.
2. Confirm with the deal team the expected annualised contract value so we can sanity-check the USD 1,000,000 figure against a twelve-month fees measure before the cap language is exchanged.
3. In the same exchange, confirm that the amended cap language keys off all amounts payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms, not the first Order Form or the § 1.5 "Fees" definition, so the definitional narrowing is not reintroduced by cross-reference.
4. Flag internally that both open items are gating: we do not recommend signature while the § 21.1 cap base and § 7.7 remain as drafted.
5. No comments required on the remaining 16 rules; we will accept those clauses as drafted.

*This memo reflects only the verified findings supplied to us and the sections cited above. One finding (§ 7.7) was recorded as repaired on verification and one (§ 21) as failing verification; we have treated both as live deviations requiring redline.*"}
